faqs.a: Points = calories/50 + fat/12 - fiber/5, with fiber capped at 4 grams, rounded to the nearest whole number. The original system assigned each person a daily Points target based on weight and activity, and dieters stayed within it. This calculator only computes the food's value, not your personal budget.
faqs.q: How did the classic Points system work?

faqs.a: Fat is calorie-dense - about 9 kcal per gram versus 4 for protein and carbohydrates - so the formula penalizes it harder than raw calories alone would. Two foods with the same calories can have different Points if one is much fattier.
faqs.q: Why does fat count extra on top of calories?

faqs.a: Yes. Fiber beyond 4 grams no longer lowers the value - the cap is baked into the classic formula. A bowl with 8 g of fiber gets the same credit as one with 4 g. Enter any number; the calculator applies the cap automatically.
faqs.q: Is there a limit to the fiber credit?

faqs.a: Not exactly. PointsPlus (2010) and later SmartPoints and Points systems use completely different formulas based on protein, carbs, sugar, and saturated fat. This calculator covers only the classic formula, which is still the one most old cookbooks and charts reference.
faqs.q: Is this the same as today's commercial points programs?

faqs.a: A banana (105 kcal, 0.4 g fat, 3.1 g fiber) is about 2 Points: 2.10 + 0.03 - 0.62 = 1.51, rounding to 2. A 300 kcal muffin with 12 g fat and 1 g fiber is 6 + 1 - 0.2 = 6.8, rounding to 7.
faqs.q: What is an example of high and low Points food?

faqs.a: Rounding moves borderline values: 2.51 becomes 3, 2.49 becomes 2. That is how the classic system worked - fractions were never tracked. The breakdown section shows the unrounded value so you can see how close a food sits to the edge.
faqs.q: Does rounding change the result much?

weight-watchers-points-calculator.formula:
Points = calories/50 + fat(g)/12 - fiber(g)/5.
Fiber is capped at 4 g for the credit.
The result is rounded to the nearest whole number (minimum 0).
Example: 300 kcal, 10 g fat, 5 g fiber -> 6 + 0.83 - 0.80 = 6.03 -> 6 points.
howTo: Enter the calories (kcal) from the nutrition label or recipe.
Enter dietary fiber in grams. The calculator caps the fiber credit at 4 g automatically.
Read the Points value instantly, with a breakdown of how each nutrient contributed.
Compare foods before you eat: for similar calories, the one with less fat and more fiber usually scores lower.
keyFacts: Classic Points = calories/50 + fat/12 - fiber/5, rounded to the nearest whole number.
Only the first 4 grams of fiber count toward the fiber credit.
Fat is penalized extra because it packs about 9 kcal per gram - more than double protein or carbs.
The classic system is the pre-2010 formula; newer commercial points programs use different formulas.
Points measure energy density for comparison, not complete nutrition - vitamins and minerals do not enter the formula.
This tool is an unofficial, independent estimate.

weight-watchers-points-calculator.workedExample:
300 kcal, 10 g fat, 5 g fiber:
1. From calories: 300 / 50 = 6.00.
2. From fat: 10 / 12 = 0.83.
3. Fiber credit: fiber is capped at 4 g, so 4 / 5 = 0.80 credit.
4. Unrounded total: 6.00 + 0.83 - 0.80 = 6.03.
5. Rounded to the nearest whole number: 6 Points.
Note: entering 8 g of fiber would give the same result, because the 4 g cap applies.
